The Upside (2017)
The Upside (2017) is a comedy-drama starring Kevin Hart and Bryan Cranston that follows two men from completely different worlds who unexpectedly develop a life-changing friendship. Dell, a struggling former convict trying to rebuild his life, is hired to become the caregiver of Phillip, a wealthy quadriplegic who has become frustrated with his isolated and dependent life.
At first, the two seem like an unlikely match. Dell has little experience as a caregiver and is mainly looking for a job, while Phillip is skeptical of Dell's attitude and unconventional approach. Their relationship begins with constant misunderstandings and disagreements, but as they spend more time together, they slowly begin to see past their differences.
Dell brings humor, energy, and a sense of freedom into Phillip's life, while Phillip gives Dell an opportunity to become more responsible and start believing in himself. Their friendship grows as they challenge each other to step outside their comfort zones and confront the parts of their lives they have been avoiding.
The film explores themes of friendship, disability, forgiveness, second chances, loneliness, responsibility, and personal growth. It shows how two people who appear to have nothing in common can still understand each other's struggles and help one another become better versions of themselves.
What makes The Upside meaningful is that neither character simply "saves" the other. Instead, their friendship gives both men something they were missing. Dell finds purpose and motivation, while Phillip begins reconnecting with life instead of allowing his circumstances to define him.
More than just a comedy, The Upside is a story about unexpected friendship and the power of giving someone another chance. Sometimes the person who enters your life by accident can end up changing it completely.
💬 Do you believe the best friendships can come from the most unexpected people?

source_details.synopsis: The Upside is a 2017 American comedy drama film directed by Neil Burger, written by Jon Hartmere. It is a remake of the French 2011 film The Intouchables, which was itself inspired by the lives of Abdel Sellou and Philippe Pozzo di Borgo. The film follows a paralyzed billionaire (Bryan Cranston) who strikes up an unlikely friendship with a recently paroled convict (Kevin Hart) whom he hires to take care of him. Nicole Kidman, Golshifteh Farahani, and Julianna Margulies also star. It is the third remake of The Intouchables after the Indian film Oopiri and the Argentinian film Inseparables (both in 2016).
